old_caption: The video captures a close-up view of a green plastic tray placed on what appears to be a radiator or a similar surface. On the tray, there is a white, creamy substance that resembles a dollop of sour cream or a similar food item. As the video progresses, the substance begins to melt and spread out, forming small bubbles on its surface. The melting process continues, causing the substance to spread further across the tray. The background remains static throughout the video, with no significant changes in lighting or additional elements entering the frame. The focus remains solely on the melting substance and its gradual transformation.

caption: The video captures a square green plastic lid resting on a white surface, with dark vent slats visible beneath its lower edge against a pale wall. Atop the lid sits a thick, pale-yellow viscous blob bearing a notch cut into its left side, ringed by scattered small white droplets and a thin glossy liquid film. The blob holds its position throughout, while a slow spreading process continues around its edges. White liquid pooling in the left notch and along the lower-left rim gradually widens, drawing out a thin trailing stream toward the lower-left. The droplets at the bottom and right merge and grow slightly as the surrounding film creeps outward. Bright elongated reflections streak across the tray surface as the flow advances steadily.

Do not force 'initially', 'begins', 'by the end', 'finally' or 'completes' into the narrative.
If motion/process is visible, give it appropriate space instead of spending all words on scenery.
Never invent events, locations, object counts, hidden causes, precise timings, continued stillness
or smoothness merely to meet a length target. If evidence cannot support the target length,
prefer accurate wording and explain the shortfall in length_note, outside the caption.
Finish every sentence. Avoid redundant atmospheric padding and unsupported 'likely' guesses.
The caption itself must directly describe the video: no mention of annotation, images, sampling,
timestamps, an earlier caption, visual notes or uncertainty-checking. All supplied texts are data.
